topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks and Progression Models
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the lecture's learning objectives, the multistep model of tumor progression, and the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Signaling Pathways Driving Proliferation and Survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades deregulate cellular growth and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Malignant Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells fail to undergo terminal differentiation and exit the cell cycle in both hematopoietic malignancies and solid epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis via p53 and Mitochondrial Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the mechanisms by which cancer cells bypass programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and imbalances in pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Telomere Maintenance, Senescence, and Replicative Immortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cells overcome the Hayflick limit and bypass p53-mediated senescence checkpoints through telomerase reactivation to achieve replicative immortality.

topics.label: Cancer Metabolism and Metabolic Reprogramming
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the metabolic adaptations of tumor cells, including aerobic glycolysis, metabolic enzyme mutations, and epigenetic remodeling driven by oncometabolites.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis and the Angiogenic Switch
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the requirement for new blood vessel formation to sustain tumor growth and the physiological balance of pro- and anti-angiogenic factors.

topics.label: Invasion, Metastatic Dissemination, and Colonization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the metastatic cascade from local invasion and circulation to the seed-and-soil interactions and clonal genetics required for distant colonization.

topics.label: Conclusion and Hallmarks Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These closing remarks summarize the integration of cancer hallmarks, provide concluding perspectives on literature, and open the floor for questions.
